findings.title: Discover upsampling is enabled for mixed or negated event-type queries
findings.body: The discover eligibility check is a raw substring match for `event.type:error`, which does not establish that the query contains only error events. Queries such as `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction` and `!event.type:error` both match and will replace `count()` with `sum(sample_weight)`. Transaction rows do not have error sampling weights, so their events are omitted or incorrectly weighted, producing incorrect counts. Parse/inspect the query condition and enable this only when it constrains the result set exclusively to error events.

findings.title: Upsampling eligibility is evaluated against the outer dataset rather than the dataset being queried
findings.body: `_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset`, including calls made for dashboard discover splits, but passes the closed-over original `dataset` to `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`. For example, a metrics-enhanced dashboard that is split into a `discover` error query evaluates eligibility as a metrics dataset and never applies upsampling. The decision needs to use `scoped_dataset` so the columns match the actual query being executed.

findings.title: Upsampled counts truncate fractional sample weights
findings.body: The custom aggregate wraps `sum(sample_weight)` in `toInt64`. Sample weights derived from arbitrary client sampling rates are not necessarily integral (for example, a 0.3 sample rate produces an expected weight near 3.33), so truncating the aggregate silently undercounts sampled errors. Return the sum as a numeric/float result unless the stored sample-weight contract guarantees integral values.

findings.title: Aliased count aggregations are not upsampled
findings.body: Only a column whose entire text is exactly `count()` is transformed. Valid selected aggregations such as `count() as errors` remain raw counts even when every project is allowlisted, yielding inconsistent and incorrect results depending solely on whether the caller aliases the aggregation. Preserve and transform supported count aliases (and their output aliases) when rewriting query columns.

findings.title: Allowlist changes leave cached count behavior stale with no invalidation integration
findings.body: Eligibility is cached for 60 seconds, and although `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is provided, this PR does not connect it to changes of `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist`. Consequently, enabling or disabling a project can continue returning raw or upsampled counts until TTL expiry, including returning upsampled counts after sampling has been disabled. Invalidate affected keys when the option changes, or avoid caching configuration whose changes must take effect immediately.
